description: CPU, GPU, disk, memory and swap usage in the status bar, as coloured progress bars with live values.
config.refreshSeconds: Display refresh interval, in seconds. Minimum 1, maximum 60.
config.barWidth: Width of each bar, in cells. Minimum 4, maximum 20.
config.alignment: Side of the status bar where the groups are shown.
config.alignment.left: Left side of the status bar.
config.alignment.right: Right side of the status bar.
config.showCpu: Show the CPU group, average load of every logical core.
config.showGpu: Show the GPU group, 3D engine utilisation. Windows through typeperf, Linux through sysfs or nvidia-smi, macOS through ioreg.
config.showDisk: Show the disk groups, one per physical disk. Windows and Linux only: macOS exposes no busy percentage without privileges.
config.showRam: Show the RAM group, system memory in use against total memory.
config.showSwap: Show the SWAP group: paging file on Windows, swap on Linux and macOS.
config.ramValue: What the RAM group displays next to its bar.
config.ramValue.used: Used against total, for example 12.35 / 31.74 GB.
config.ramValue.free: Free memory only, for example 19.39 GB free. On Linux this is MemAvailable, which counts reclaimable cache as free.
config.diskDevices: Disks shown in the status bar, one group per disk (for example ["0 C:"] on Windows, ["sda"] on Linux). Empty shows every disk seen. Easiest to fill through the command System Monitor: Choose the disks shown.
config.cpuDevices: CPU groups shown: "all" for the average of every core, then one logical core number per group (for example ["all", "0", "1"]). Empty shows the average alone. Filled by the command System Monitor: Choose the CPU cores shown.
config.gpuDevices: GPU groups shown: "all" for the sum of every adapter, then one group per GPU ("0", "1" on Windows and with nvidia-smi, "card0" on Linux). Empty shows the sum alone. Filled by the command System Monitor: Choose the GPUs shown.
config.showLabels: Show the label of each group (CPU, GPU, DISK, RAM, SWAP).
config.showBars: Show the progress bar of each group.
config.showValues: Show the numeric value of each group.
config.probeRestartSeconds: Recycle interval of the GPU/disk probe, in seconds. On Windows, typeperf freezes its instance set at startup, and recycling picks up new processes. On Linux, recycling runs GPU detection again, useful when a driver loads late.
config.tooltipSeconds: How often tooltips are rebuilt, in seconds. VS Code does not refresh a tooltip while it is shown, so rebuilding it on every tick serves nobody.
config.shareProbe: Share a single probe between every VS Code window, through a lease file in the temp directory. One window measures, the others read its result.
config.pauseWhenUnfocused: Stop the probe while the window has no focus. VS Code can tell whether a window is active but not whether it is visible, so a window shown on a second screen greys out. Probe sharing makes this setting unnecessary in most cases.
config.unfocusedMultiplier: Factor applied to the refresh interval while the window has no focus. 1 keeps the same pace everywhere, so a window visible on a second screen does not lag behind.
